+# Midnight Club: Los Angeles — native car files
+
+Extracted from the supplied Xbox 360 disc image, Complete Edition (USA, Europe). The original
+`.7z` and the ISO unpacked from it remain under `game-files/` and are never committed or edited:
+
+| File | Bytes | SHA-256 |
+| --- | ---: | --- |
+| `Midnight Club - Los Angeles - Complete Edition (USA, Europe).7z` | 6,612,480,974 | `cadd0f7b71bc888435793fd9d2fde68d1667a01d6f146592846b5487317986e8` |
+| `Midnight Club - Los Angeles - Complete Edition (USA, Europe).iso` | 7,838,695,424 | `877a9415f695d27f8170d04d3f18aab13e2b4de3cbabda824e04c9338b2914e9` |
+
+The ISO's SHA-1 (`4ca07fcf…b263`) equals the Redump value on the archive's own `Vimm's Lair.txt`.
+The image was unpacked with `bsdtar -xf <archive>` (libarchive, stock on macOS).
+
+Car data sits in the disc's `xarchive_cache.rpf`, an RPF3 archive with an AES-encrypted table and
+hashed names. The repo-owned readers decrypt `default.xex`, locate the archive key in it by its
+SHA-256 pin (the key itself is never written out), decrypt the table and recover names from strings
+found on the same disc.
+
+`cars/` holds **106 cars** (one per directory under `resources/vehicle/`) and **10,702 files**
+totaling **415,232,242 bytes**. Only `index.json` (every file's SHA-256) and `provenance/` are
+committed; the rest is local and re-derived from the disc (see `.gitignore`):
+
+```text
+cars/
+  index.json                         disc identity, archive summary, name statistics, every file hash
+  <code>/manifest.json               per-file archive path, name hash and source, offsets, stored SHA-256, role
+  <code>/resources/vehicle/<code>/   the car's package: RSC5 model parts, tuning (.xct), streaming map (.xspm),
+                                     part/damage textures (.xtp/.xtl)
+  <code>/resources/vehicle/configs/  car configurations whose name contains the code (.xcc)
+  <code>/resources/ambients/<code>/  ambient-traffic definition (va_ cars)
+  <code>/resources/ui/textures/garage/...  garage, showroom and reward textures naming the code
+  shared/resources/{rims,tires,brakes}/    wheels, tires and brakes; owners not inferred
+  shared/vehicle/, shared/tune/vehicle/    shared vehicle effects and vehicle tuning
+  shared/resources/vehicle/configs/        configurations naming no car code
+  provenance/disc.inventory.json           complete XDVDFS listing
+  provenance/<archive>.rpf.inventory.json  every decrypted RPF3 table with recovered names
+  provenance/archive-key.json              key SHA-256 and its location in the executable image
+```
+
+Car IDs are directory names: 49 `vp_`, 16 `vpd_` and 41 `va_`. Reading the prefixes as player,
+downloadable-content player and ambient traffic is an interpretation; IDs are not decoded retail names. The disc carries the code `vp_nsn_gtr_08`
+only inside the garage texture name `mr_vp_nsn_gtr_08` (other strings spell it `vpd_nsn_gtr_08`).
+About 94% of the 9,273 files inside car packages keep `0x<hash>` names because no disc string hashes
+to them; resource-type extensions (for example `.xrsc` for type 63) are borrowed only where every
+resolved name of that type agrees.
+
+From the repository root:
+
+```sh
+python3 tools/extract_mcla_cars.py --check
+```
+
+The check reads the ISO again and rejects changed, missing, extra or linked output. Initial
+extraction uses the same command without `--check`, into a new or empty destination (`--output`
+chooses another one). It never overwrites.
+
+## Not established
+
+RSC5 resources keep their stored Xbox 360 LZX compression; no model, texture or tuning data is
+decoded, and nothing is converted to GLB or added to the catalogs. Part names, runtime dependency
+closure, shared wheel ownership and game-render fidelity remain open. See
+[the extraction note](../research/midnight-club-los-angeles-extraction.md) for format sources,
+verification and open items.

+# Midnight Club: Los Angeles native car extraction
+
+Date: 2026-10-12. Scope: set up `midnight-club-los-angeles/` from the supplied archive and extract
+the game's native car files into `midnight-club-los-angeles/cars/`. No geometry or texture decoding.
+Receipt: [`evidence/midnight-club-los-angeles/extraction.json`](evidence/midnight-club-los-angeles/extraction.json).
+
+## Input
+
+| Fact | Value | How established |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Archive | `Midnight Club - Los Angeles - Complete Edition (USA, Europe).7z`, 6,612,480,974 bytes, SHA-256 `cadd0f7b…7986e8` | moved from `~/Downloads` into `game-files/`; hashed locally |
+| Disc image | the archive's only image member, 7,838,695,424 bytes, SHA-256 `877a9415…2914e9`, SHA-1 `4ca07fcf…b263` | unpacked with `bsdtar -xf`; SHA-1 equals the Redump value in the archive's `Vimm's Lair.txt`; pinned in `cars/index.json` |
+| Platform | Xbox 360, XGD2 layout: XDVDFS volume descriptor at partition offset `0xFD90000`, sector 32 | `MICROSOFT*XBOX*MEDIA` at both ends of the descriptor; the image size is the XGD2 size |
+| Disc contents | 16 entries: `default.xex`, four RPF3 archives, Bink videos, a system update | `provenance/disc.inventory.json` |
+
+## Formats
+
+Sources (format reference only; no code was copied — neither repository declares a licence):
+
+- [Foxxyyy/CodeX.Games.MCLA](https://github.com/Foxxyyy/CodeX.Games.MCLA) at `dedc3156`: `RPF3/Rpf3File.cs`
+  (header, entry layout, resource flags), `RPF3/Rpf3Crypto.cs` (sixteen AES-256-ECB passes).
+- [Raskulk/MCLA-Tools](https://github.com/Raskulk/MCLA-Tools) at `68419cee`: README and `xrsc2obj.py`
+  header comments (RSC5 container with Xbox 360 LZX body).
+- [GTAMods RPF archive](https://gtamods.com/wiki/RPF_archive): RPF3 is the GTA IV audio / MCLA version.
+- XEX2 retail key and header layout as used by the Xenia emulator (`xe_xex2_retail_key`).
+
+All seven fetched source texts were screened with `jev_screen` before use (injection ≤ 0.03; the
+three CodeX RPF3 files passed as relevant, the READMEs and the xrsc header were marked not relevant
+and were not relied on). Receipt: [`source-screens.json`](evidence/midnight-club-los-angeles/source-screens.json)
+records digests of the exact screened text, not the text.
+
+What the repo-owned readers implement, and what the real disc confirmed:
+
+1. **XDVDFS** (`tools/xdvdfs.py`): directory binary trees of 4-byte-aligned records (left/right
+   offsets in dwords, sector, size, attributes, name). Records never cross a sector. The reader rejects
+   cycles, unsafe or duplicate names, extents outside the image and overlapping files.
+2. **XEX2** (`tools/xex2.py`): `default.xex` has normal (AES) encryption and **basic** packing
+   (two blocks, 8,617,984 + 622,592 stored bytes with a 1,114,112-byte zero fill), so no LZX is needed.
+   The session key is the file key decrypted under the retail key; the image is AES-128-CBC with a zero
+   IV. The result starts with `MZ`, has a PE header and is exactly the declared 0x9E0000 bytes.
+3. **Archive key**: the 32-byte RPF3 key occurs exactly once in the decrypted image, at offset
+   `0x7D8AC4`. The tool finds it by SHA-256 (`71f5abd8…5b505c`) over 4-byte-aligned windows; only the
+   digest and offset are recorded (`provenance/archive-key.json`). The pin was taken from the CodeX
+   key literal and confirmed by its single occurrence in the disc executable and by the decrypted tables
+   passing every structural check below.
+4. **RPF3** (`tools/mcla_rpf.py`): little-endian header `RPF3`, table size, entry count, unknown word,
+   encryption flag (−1 on all four archives); table at 0x800, AES-256-ECB applied sixteen times. 16-byte
+   entries: directories (third word has bit 31) give first child and count; files give size, offset and a
+   flag word. Both top flag bits mark an RSC resource whose offset carries the resource type in its low
+   byte; otherwise bit 30 marks raw DEFLATE. The reader requires a root directory, contiguous children
+   after their parent, exactly one parent per entry, every entry reachable, extents inside the archive,
+   exact DEFLATE sizes and the `\x05CSR` (RSC5) header on every resource. Decryption is pure Python
+   (`tools/aes_decrypt.py`, FIPS-197 and SP 800-38A vectors) because the stock interpreter has no
+   crypto module.
+5. **Names** are Jenkins one-at-a-time hashes of lower-cased names; none are stored. Names are
+   recovered from 448,917 printable strings harvested from the executable image and the cache
+   archive's loose members, offered as-is, with a known extension, and (for strings such as
+   `mr_vp_nsn_gtr_08`) as an embedded car code. A candidate must agree with its entry: directories take
+   no dotted name, resources take a resource extension, loose files do not. An entry is named only when
+   exactly one plausible candidate remains. The first run, without those rules, named directories and
+   files with binary noise such as `-tm2.xlm`, `w3hu.dds` and `anaj.xbtm`; with them, 7,426 of 23,931
+   cache entries are named; 8 hashes have more than one raw candidate and 3 cache entries keep several plausible ones. A remaining collision is possible and
+   stays a claim limit.
+
+## Car files
+
+`xarchive_cache.rpf` (2,130,739,200 bytes, 23,931 entries) holds all car data under
+`resources/vehicle/<code>/`: 49 `vp_`, 16 `vpd_` and 41 `va_` directories plus `configs/`. One
+directory hashes to no harvested string directly; the embedded-code rule names it `vp_nsn_gtr_08`
+from the garage texture `mr_vp_nsn_gtr_08` (the same hash appears in an external CodeX name list,
+which the tool does not use). The prefix readings (player, downloadable-content player, ambient
+traffic) are interpretations.
+
+| Resource type | Files in car packages | Resolved extension | Reading (CodeX type table) |
+| ---: | ---: | --- | --- |
+| 63 | 8,849 | `.xrsc` (only `body_lod_0.xrsc` resolves by name) | model resource parts |
+| 83 | 212 | `.xtp`, `.xtl` | part and damage textures |
+| 50 | 106 | `.xct` | car tuning |
+| 19 | 106 | `.xspm` | streaming pack map |
+
+Selection (`tools/extract_mcla_cars.py`) is a declared namespace boundary: a car takes its vehicle
+directory, its `resources/ambients/<code>/` directory, and the configs and garage UI textures whose
+file name contains its full code as an underscore-delimited run (the longest code wins, so
+`sh_vp_lam_murcielago_06_dub` goes to the `_dub` car). Rims, tires, brakes, `vehicle/` effects,
+`tune/vehicle/` and configs naming no code go to `shared/`. The other three archives (audio, low audio,
+music) and the preload copy `preload/xarchive_carconfigs.rpf` (a nested RPF3 duplicating the configs)
+are inventoried, not extracted. Result: 106 cars, 10,702 output files, 415,232,242 bytes; 94.3% of the
+9,273 car-package files keep `0x<hash>` names.
+
+RSC5 resources are written exactly as stored (their LZX-compressed body included); DEFLATE members
+are written inflated, with the stored SHA-256 kept in each manifest.
+
+## Verification
+
+| Command | Result |
+| --- | --- |
+| `python3 tools/extract_mcla_cars.py` | `EXTRACTED 106 cars, 10702 files, 415232242 bytes` (35 s) |
+| `python3 tools/extract_mcla_cars.py --check` | `CHECKED 106 cars, 10702 files, 415232242 bytes`, also under stock Python 3.9.6 |
+| `test_aes_decrypt`, `test_xdvdfs`, `test_xex2`, `test_mcla_rpf`, `test_extract_mcla_cars` | synthetic encrypted disc, XEX and archive with tamper controls: wrong key, unreachable or doubly-parented entries, bad DEFLATE sizes, missing RSC5 header, overlapping extents, unexpected vehicle directory, rewritten index masking a payload change, extra and linked output |
+
+`mcla_extraction` in `tools/check.sh` runs the full re-derivation only where the ISO is present.
+
+## Not established
+
+- RSC5/LZX decoding: no model, texture, tuning or streaming-map content is read, so part names inside
+  `.xspm` maps, geometry, materials and wheel placement are unknown. No GLB conversion; the cars are not
+  in either catalog yet.
+- Ownership of shared rims, tires and brakes, runtime dependency closure and load precedence.
+- Meaning of the RPF3 header's unknown word and of the per-directory flag words.
+- Anything about the PS3 release or other builds; only this Xbox 360 disc was read.

+"""Pure-Python AES decryption (FIPS-197) for the stock interpreter, which has no crypto module.
+
+Decryption only: ECB and CBC over whole 16-byte blocks. Checked against the FIPS-197
+appendix C vectors in test_aes_decrypt.py. Speed is adequate for archive tables and one
+executable image; it is not constant-time and must never handle secrets of this repo.
+"""
+
+
+def _tables():
+    sbox, inverse = [0] * 256, [0] * 256
+    p = q = 1
+    while True:
+        p ^= (p << 1) ^ (0x1B if p & 0x80 else 0)
+        p &= 0xFF
+        q ^= q << 1
+        q ^= q << 2
+        q ^= q << 4
+        q &= 0xFF
+        if q & 0x80:
+            q ^= 0x09
+        value = q ^ ((q << 1 | q >> 7) & 0xFF) ^ ((q << 2 | q >> 6) & 0xFF) ^ ((q << 3 | q >> 5) & 0xFF) \
+            ^ ((q << 4 | q >> 4) & 0xFF) ^ 0x63
+        sbox[p] = value
+        inverse[value] = p
+        if p == 1:
+            break
+    sbox[0], inverse[0x63] = 0x63, 0
+
+    def mul(a, b):
+        out = 0
+        while b:
+            if b & 1:
+                out ^= a
+            a = ((a << 1) ^ (0x1B if a & 0x80 else 0)) & 0xFF
+            b >>= 1
+        return out
+    decrypt = [[0] * 256 for _ in range(4)]
+    for x in range(256):
+        s = inverse[x]
+        word = (mul(s, 14) << 24) | (mul(s, 9) << 16) | (mul(s, 13) << 8) | mul(s, 11)
+        for r in range(4):
+            decrypt[r][x] = ((word >> (8 * r)) | (word << (32 - 8 * r))) & 0xFFFFFFFF
+    mix = [[0] * 256 for _ in range(4)]  # InvMixColumns of a plain byte, for the key schedule
+    for x in range(256):
+        word = (mul(x, 14) << 24) | (mul(x, 9) << 16) | (mul(x, 13) << 8) | mul(x, 11)
+        for r in range(4):
+            mix[r][x] = ((word >> (8 * r)) | (word << (32 - 8 * r))) & 0xFFFFFFFF
+    return sbox, inverse, decrypt, mix
+
+
+SBOX, INVERSE, TD, MIX = _tables()
+RCON = [0x01, 0x02, 0x04, 0x08, 0x10, 0x20, 0x40, 0x80, 0x1B, 0x36]
+
+
+class AesDecryptor:
+    def __init__(self, key):
+        if len(key) not in (16, 24, 32):
+            raise ValueError('AES key must be 16, 24 or 32 bytes')
+        nk = len(key) // 4
+        self.rounds = nk + 6
+        words = [int.from_bytes(key[4 * i:4 * i + 4], 'big') for i in range(nk)]
+        for i in range(nk, 4 * (self.rounds + 1)):
+            t = words[i - 1]
+            if i % nk == 0:
+                t = ((t << 8) | (t >> 24)) & 0xFFFFFFFF
+                t = (SBOX[t >> 24] << 24) | (SBOX[t >> 16 & 255] << 16) | (SBOX[t >> 8 & 255] << 8) | SBOX[t & 255]
+                t ^= RCON[i // nk - 1] << 24
+            elif nk > 6 and i % nk == 4:
+                t = (SBOX[t >> 24] << 24) | (SBOX[t >> 16 & 255] << 16) | (SBOX[t >> 8 & 255] << 8) | SBOX[t & 255]
+            words.append(words[i - nk] ^ t)
+        # Equivalent inverse cipher: reversed round keys, InvMixColumns on the middle ones.
+        keys = [words[4 * r:4 * r + 4] for r in range(self.rounds + 1)][::-1]
+        for r in range(1, self.rounds):
+            keys[r] = [MIX[0][w >> 24] ^ MIX[1][w >> 16 & 255] ^ MIX[2][w >> 8 & 255] ^ MIX[3][w & 255]
+                       for w in keys[r]]
+        self.keys = keys
+
+    def block(self, data):
+        k = self.keys
+        t0, t1, t2, t3 = TD
+        s0 = int.from_bytes(data[0:4], 'big') ^ k[0][0]
+        s1 = int.from_bytes(data[4:8], 'big') ^ k[0][1]
+        s2 = int.from_bytes(data[8:12], 'big') ^ k[0][2]
+        s3 = int.from_bytes(data[12:16], 'big') ^ k[0][3]
+        for r in range(1, self.rounds):
+            rk = k[r]
+            s0, s1, s2, s3 = (
+                t0[s0 >> 24] ^ t1[s3 >> 16 & 255] ^ t2[s2 >> 8 & 255] ^ t3[s1 & 255] ^ rk[0],
+                t0[s1 >> 24] ^ t1[s0 >> 16 & 255] ^ t2[s3 >> 8 & 255] ^ t3[s2 & 255] ^ rk[1],
+                t0[s2 >> 24] ^ t1[s1 >> 16 & 255] ^ t2[s0 >> 8 & 255] ^ t3[s3 & 255] ^ rk[2],
+                t0[s3 >> 24] ^ t1[s2 >> 16 & 255] ^ t2[s1 >> 8 & 255] ^ t3[s0 & 255] ^ rk[3])
+        rk, inv = k[self.rounds], INVERSE
+        out = (
+            ((inv[s0 >> 24] << 24) | (inv[s3 >> 16 & 255] << 16) | (inv[s2 >> 8 & 255] << 8) | inv[s1 & 255]) ^ rk[0],
+            ((inv[s1 >> 24] << 24) | (inv[s0 >> 16 & 255] << 16) | (inv[s3 >> 8 & 255] << 8) | inv[s2 & 255]) ^ rk[1],
+            ((inv[s2 >> 24] << 24) | (inv[s1 >> 16 & 255] << 16) | (inv[s0 >> 8 & 255] << 8) | inv[s3 & 255]) ^ rk[2],
+            ((inv[s3 >> 24] << 24) | (inv[s2 >> 16 & 255] << 16) | (inv[s1 >> 8 & 255] << 8) | inv[s0 & 255]) ^ rk[3])
+        return b''.join(w.to_bytes(4, 'big') for w in out)
+
+    def ecb(self, data):
+        if len(data) % 16:
+            raise ValueError('AES input is not whole blocks')
+        return b''.join(self.block(data[i:i + 16]) for i in range(0, len(data), 16))
+
+    def cbc(self, data, iv=bytes(16)):
+        if len(data) % 16 or len(iv) != 16:
+            raise ValueError('AES input is not whole blocks')
+        out, previous = bytearray(), iv
+        for i in range(0, len(data), 16):
+            chunk = data[i:i + 16]
+            plain = int.from_bytes(self.block(chunk), 'big') ^ int.from_bytes(previous, 'big')
+            out += plain.to_bytes(16, 'big')
+            previous = chunk
+        return bytes(out)

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Extract Midnight Club: Los Angeles native car files from the supplied Xbox 360 disc image.
+
+The disc is XDVDFS; car data sits in the RPF3 archive `xarchive_cache.rpf`, whose table is
+AES-encrypted. The key is located inside the disc's own `default.xex` image by its SHA-256
+pin, so no key is stored in this repository. Archive names are hashes; names are recovered
+only from strings found on the same disc. Selection is a declared namespace boundary, not
+inferred runtime closure. RSC5 resources stay as stored (LZX-compressed); --check derives
+every output again from the disc. No geometry or texture conversion.
+"""
+import argparse
+import hashlib
+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+import re
+import tempfile
+import zlib
+
+from mc3_archive import safe_name
+from mcla_rpf import Rpf3Archive, jenkins_final, jenkins_partial
+from xdvdfs import XdvdfsDisc
+from xex2 import load_image
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
+GAME = 'Midnight Club: Los Angeles'
+DEFAULT_ISO = ROOT / 'midnight-club-los-angeles/game-files/Midnight Club - Los Angeles - Complete Edition (USA, Europe).iso'
+KEY_SHA256 = '71f5abd83015a713952b7c2f2c25289f92f3cf9a9dd740c40a511a62ea5b505c'
+CACHE = 'xarchive_cache.rpf'
+VEHICLES = 'resources/vehicle/'
+CONFIGS = VEHICLES + 'configs/'
+AMBIENTS = 'resources/ambients/'
+UI = 'resources/ui/textures/garage/'
+SHARED = ('resources/rims/', 'resources/tires/', 'resources/brakes/', 'vehicle/', 'tune/vehicle/')
+CODE = re.compile(r'v(?:a|p|pd)_[a-z0-9_]+')
+# File extensions tried after recovered stems: a reading of the resource-type table in
+# CodeX.Games.MCLA plus loose-file extensions seen in recovered names.
+RESOURCE_EXTENSIONS = ('xrsc', 'xtp', 'xtl', 'xspm', 'xct', 'xtd', 'xdr', 'xft', 'xwt', 'xshp', 'xcs', 'xapk',
+                       'xmd', 'xbtm', 'xsf', 'xaph', 'xapb', 'xck', 'xmp', 'xlm')
+EXTENSIONS = RESOURCE_EXTENSIONS + ('xcc', 'mesh', 'type', 'dds', 'xml')
+TOKEN = re.compile(rb'[A-Za-z0-9_./\\\-]{3,120}')
+STEM = re.compile(r'[a-z0-9_\-]{1,100}')
+LIMITS = [
+    'Native archive extraction only; RSC5 resources keep their stored LZX compression. Model, texture and '
+    'tuning decoding, GLB conversion and rendering remain unverified.',
+    'Car IDs are vehicle directory names under resources/vehicle/ (vp_ player, vpd_ downloadable-content '
+    'player, va_ ambient), not decoded retail names or a verified playable roster.',
+    'Archive names are 32-bit hashes. A name is resolved only when exactly one plausible string harvested from '
+    'this disc hashes to it; other entries keep 0x<hash> names. A resolved name can still be a hash collision.',
+    'Configs and garage UI textures join a car only when its full code occurs in the file name; rims, tires, '
+    'brakes, shared vehicle effects and vehicle tuning are shared with ownership unknown.',
+    'Selection is a declared namespace boundary; runtime dependency closure and load precedence are unknown.',
+    'Checks establish byte extraction and source preservation, not game execution or visual fidelity.',
+]
+
+
+def sha(data):
+    return hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()
+
+
+def json_bytes(value):
+    return (json.dumps(value, indent=1, sort_keys=True) + '\n').encode()
+
+
+def source_digests(path):
+    sha256, sha1 = hashlib.sha256(), hashlib.sha1()
+    with Path(path).open('rb') as stream:
+        while chunk := stream.read(8 * 1024 * 1024):
+            sha256.update(chunk)
+            sha1.update(chunk)
+    return sha256.hexdigest(), sha1.hexdigest()
+
+
+def locate_key(image):
+    """The single 4-byte-aligned 32-byte window of the executable image matching the pin."""
+    hits = [at for at in range(0, len(image) - 31, 4) if sha(image[at:at + 32]) == KEY_SHA256]
+    if len(hits) != 1:
+        raise ValueError('archive key not found exactly once in default.xex')
+    return image[hits[0]:hits[0] + 32], hits[0]
+
+
+def harvest(blobs):
+    """Lower-cased names and path components found as printable runs in the supplied bytes."""
+    names = set()
+    for blob in blobs:
+        for match in TOKEN.findall(blob):
+            text = match.decode('ascii').lower().replace('\\', '/')
+            names.add(text)
+            names.update(text.split('/'))
+    names.discard('')
+    return names
+
+
+def dictionary(names, wanted):
+    """Hash -> sorted candidate names, from harvested names and stems with known extensions."""
+    found = {}
+
+    def offer(name, h):
+        if h in wanted and name not in ('.', '..'):
+            found.setdefault(h, set()).add(name)
+    stems = set()
+    for name in sorted(names):
+        offer(name, jenkins_final(jenkins_partial(name)))
+        stem = name.rsplit('.', 1)[0] if '.' in name else name
+        if STEM.fullmatch(stem):
+            stems.add(stem)
+            # A car code embedded after a prefix (mr_vp_..., msh_vpd_...) is offered on its own.
+            parts = stem.split('_')
+            for start in range(1, len(parts)):
+                suffix = '_'.join(parts[start:])
+                if CODE.fullmatch(suffix):
+                    offer(suffix, jenkins_final(jenkins_partial(suffix)))
+                    stems.add(suffix)
+    for stem in stems:
+        state = jenkins_partial(stem + '.')
+        for extension in EXTENSIONS:
+            offer(stem + '.' + extension, jenkins_final(jenkins_partial(extension, state)))
+    return {h: sorted(v) for h, v in found.items()}
+
+
+def plausible(entry, name):
+    """Structural agreement between an entry and a candidate name (rejects most hash noise)."""
+    extension = name.rsplit('.', 1)[1] if '.' in name else ''
+    if entry['kind'] == 'directory':
+        return '.' not in name
+    return (extension in RESOURCE_EXTENSIONS) == entry['resource']
+
+
+class Named:
+    """Entry names and archive paths for one RPF3 archive under the disc dictionary."""
+
+    def __init__(self, archive, names):
+        self.archive, self.names = archive, names
+        typed = {}
+        for entry in archive.entries:
+            accepted = self.accepted(entry)
+            if entry['kind'] == 'file' and entry['resource'] and len(accepted) == 1:
+                typed.setdefault(entry['resource_type'], set()).add(accepted[0].rsplit('.', 1)[1])
+        # An unresolved resource borrows an extension only when every resolved entry of its type agrees.
+        self.extension = {kind: next(iter(v)) for kind, v in typed.items() if len(v) == 1}
+        self.paths = {}
+        for entry in archive.entries:

+"""Read-only RPF3 reader for Midnight Club: Los Angeles (Xbox 360).
+
+Format readings (independently written; CodeX.Games.MCLA `RPF3/Rpf3File.cs` at
+dedc3156 was the format reference, no code copied), each checked by the reader:
+
+- Header, little-endian: `RPF3`, table size, entry count, unknown, encryption flag.
+  The table starts at 0x800. A nonzero flag means the table is AES-256-ECB
+  encrypted sixteen times over its 16-byte-aligned prefix.
+- 16-byte entries. A negative third word marks a directory: name hash, flags,
+  first child index | 0x80000000, child count. Otherwise a file: name hash,
+  size, offset, flag word. Flag bits 0xC0000000 both set mark an RSC resource
+  whose offset carries the resource type in its low byte; otherwise bit
+  0x40000000 marks raw-DEFLATE compression and the rest is the stored size.
+- Names are 32-bit Jenkins one-at-a-time hashes; no names are stored.
+"""
+import struct
+import zlib
+
+from aes_decrypt import AesDecryptor
+
+MAGIC = b'RPF3'
+TOC_OFFSET = 0x800
+ENTRY = 16
+MAX_ENTRIES = 1_000_000
+RESOURCE = 0xC0000000
+COMPRESSED = 0x40000000
+RSC5 = b'\x05CSR'  # reading of the resource magic as stored big-endian on this disc
+
+
+def jenkins_partial(text, h=0):
+    """Jenkins one-at-a-time mixing over lower-cased ASCII, resumable from a prefix state."""
+    for byte in text.lower().encode('ascii'):
+        h = (h + byte) & 0xFFFFFFFF
+        h = (h + (h << 10)) & 0xFFFFFFFF
+        h ^= h >> 6
+    return h
+
+
+def jenkins_final(h):
+    h = (h + (h << 3)) & 0xFFFFFFFF
+    h ^= h >> 11
+    return (h + (h << 15)) & 0xFFFFFFFF
+
+
+def jenkins(text):
+    """The RAGE name hash: Jenkins one-at-a-time over lower-cased ASCII."""
+    return jenkins_final(jenkins_partial(text))
+
+
+def aes_ecb_decrypt16(data, key):
+    """Sixteen AES-256-ECB decryption passes over the 16-byte-aligned prefix."""
+    aligned = len(data) & ~15
+    aes, body = AesDecryptor(key), data[:aligned]
+    for _ in range(16):
+        body = aes.ecb(body)
+    return body + data[aligned:]
+
+
+def virtual_size(flag):
+    return (flag & 0x7FF) << (((flag >> 11) & 15) + 8)
+
+
+def physical_size(flag):
+    return ((flag >> 15) & 0x7FF) << (((flag >> 26) & 15) + 8)
+
+
+class Rpf3Archive:
+    """Lists entries of one RPF3 image held behind `read(offset, size)`."""
+
+    def __init__(self, read, size, key=None):
+        self.read, self.size = read, size
+        if size < TOC_OFFSET:
+            raise ValueError('RPF3 smaller than its header page')
+        magic, toc_size, count, self.unknown, encrypted = struct.unpack('<4sIIIi', read(0, 20))
+        if magic != MAGIC:
+            raise ValueError('not an RPF3 archive')
+        if not 0 < count <= MAX_ENTRIES or count * ENTRY > toc_size or TOC_OFFSET + toc_size > size:
+            raise ValueError('RPF3 table outside archive')
+        self.encrypted = encrypted != 0
+        table = read(TOC_OFFSET, toc_size)
+        if self.encrypted:
+            if key is None:
+                raise ValueError('encrypted RPF3 table needs the AES key')
+            table = aes_ecb_decrypt16(table, key)
+        self.toc_size, self.count = toc_size, count
+        self.entries = [self._entry(index, table[index * ENTRY:(index + 1) * ENTRY]) for index in range(count)]
+        root = self.entries[0]
+        if root['kind'] != 'directory':
+            raise ValueError('RPF3 root is not a directory')
+        self._link()
+
+    def _entry(self, index, raw):
+        name, a, b, c = struct.unpack('<IIII', raw)
+        if b & 0x80000000:
+            return {'index': index, 'kind': 'directory', 'hash': name, 'flags': a,
+                    'first': b & 0x7FFFFFFF, 'children': c & 0x0FFFFFFF}
+        entry = {'index': index, 'kind': 'file', 'hash': name, 'size': a, 'flag': c}
+        if c & RESOURCE == RESOURCE:
+            entry.update(resource=True, resource_type=b & 0xFF, offset=b & 0x7FFFFF00,
+                         stored=a, virtual=virtual_size(c), physical=physical_size(c))
+        else:
+            entry.update(resource=False, offset=b, compressed=bool(c & COMPRESSED), stored=c & 0x3FFFFFFF)
+        if entry['offset'] + entry['stored'] > self.size:
+            raise ValueError('RPF3 file outside archive')
+        return entry
+
+    def _link(self):
+        parents = {0: None}
+        stack = [0]
+        while stack:
+            directory = self.entries[stack.pop()]
+            first, count = directory['first'], directory['children']
+            if first + count > self.count or (count and first <= directory['index']):
+                raise ValueError('RPF3 directory children outside table')
+            for child in range(first, first + count):
+                if child in parents:
+                    raise ValueError('RPF3 entry has two parents')
+                parents[child] = directory['index']
+                if self.entries[child]['kind'] == 'directory':
+                    stack.append(child)
+        if len(parents) != self.count:
+            raise ValueError('RPF3 entries unreachable from root')
+        for entry in self.entries:
+            entry['parent'] = parents[entry['index']]
+
+    def stored(self, entry):
+        return self.read(entry['offset'], entry['stored'])
+
+    def payload(self, entry):
+        """Archive-level decoding only: raw DEFLATE is inflated; RSC resources stay as stored."""
+        data = self.stored(entry)
+        if entry['resource']:
+            if data[:4] != RSC5:
+                raise ValueError('RPF3 resource without RSC5 header')
+            return data
+        if not entry['compressed']:
+            return data
+        inflater = zlib.decompressobj(-15)
+        out = inflater.decompress(data, entry['size'] + 1)
+        if len(out) != entry['size'] or inflater.unconsumed_tail or not inflater.eof:
+            raise ValueError('RPF3 deflate size mismatch')
+        return out

+"""FIPS-197 appendix C known-answer vectors, CBC chaining and malformed-input controls.
+
+`AesEncryptor` is a deliberately plain, test-only forward cipher used to build encrypted
+fixtures for the MCLA disc tests; it is checked against the same vectors.
+"""
+import unittest
+
+from aes_decrypt import SBOX, AesDecryptor
+
+
+def _xtime(a):
+    return ((a << 1) ^ (0x1B if a & 0x80 else 0)) & 0xFF
+
+
+class AesEncryptor:
+    def __init__(self, key):
+        nk = len(key) // 4
+        self.rounds = nk + 6
+        words = [list(key[4 * i:4 * i + 4]) for i in range(nk)]
+        rcon = 1
+        for i in range(nk, 4 * (self.rounds + 1)):
+            t = list(words[i - 1])
+            if i % nk == 0:
+                t = [SBOX[b] for b in t[1:] + t[:1]]
+                t[0] ^= rcon
+                rcon = _xtime(rcon)
+            elif nk > 6 and i % nk == 4:
+                t = [SBOX[b] for b in t]
+            words.append([a ^ b for a, b in zip(words[i - nk], t)])
+        self.keys = [sum(words[4 * r:4 * r + 4], []) for r in range(self.rounds + 1)]
+
+    def block(self, data):
+        s = [a ^ b for a, b in zip(data, self.keys[0])]
+        for r in range(1, self.rounds + 1):
+            s = [SBOX[b] for b in s]
+            s = [s[(i + 4 * (i % 4)) % 16] for i in range(16)]  # ShiftRows on column-major state
+            if r < self.rounds:
+                mixed = []
+                for c in range(4):
+                    a = s[4 * c:4 * c + 4]
+                    total = a[0] ^ a[1] ^ a[2] ^ a[3]
+                    mixed += [a[i] ^ total ^ _xtime(a[i] ^ a[(i + 1) % 4]) for i in range(4)]
+                s = mixed
+            s = [a ^ b for a, b in zip(s, self.keys[r])]
+        return bytes(s)
+
+    def ecb(self, data):
+        return b''.join(self.block(data[i:i + 16]) for i in range(0, len(data), 16))
+
+    def cbc(self, data, iv=bytes(16)):
+        out, previous = bytearray(), iv
+        for i in range(0, len(data), 16):
+            previous = self.block(bytes(a ^ b for a, b in zip(data[i:i + 16], previous)))
+            out += previous
+        return bytes(out)
+
+
+PLAIN = bytes.fromhex('00112233445566778899aabbccddeeff')
+VECTORS = [
+    ('000102030405060708090a0b0c0d0e0f', '69c4e0d86a7b0430d8cdb78070b4c55a'),
+    ('000102030405060708090a0b0c0d0e0f1011121314151617', 'dda97ca4864cdfe06eaf70a0ec0d7191'),
+    ('000102030405060708090a0b0c0d0e0f101112131415161718191a1b1c1d1e1f', '8ea2b7ca516745bfeafc49904b496089'),
+]
+
+
+class AesTests(unittest.TestCase):
+    def test_fips197_vectors(self):
+        for key, cipher in VECTORS:
+            self.assertEqual(AesDecryptor(bytes.fromhex(key)).block(bytes.fromhex(cipher)), PLAIN)
+
+    def test_fixture_encryptor_round_trips(self):
+        for key, cipher in VECTORS:
+            self.assertEqual(AesEncryptor(bytes.fromhex(key)).block(PLAIN).hex(), cipher)
+        key = bytes(range(32))
+        data = bytes(range(256)) * 2
+        self.assertEqual(AesDecryptor(key).cbc(AesEncryptor(key).cbc(data, b'v' * 16), b'v' * 16), data)
+
+    def test_wrong_key_does_not_decrypt(self):
+        key, cipher = VECTORS[2]
+        wrong = bytearray.fromhex(key)
+        wrong[0] ^= 1
+        self.assertNotEqual(AesDecryptor(bytes(wrong)).block(bytes.fromhex(cipher)), PLAIN)
+
+    def test_cbc_chains_previous_ciphertext(self):
+        # NIST SP 800-38A F.2.2 (CBC-AES128.Decrypt), first two blocks.
+        aes = AesDecryptor(bytes.fromhex('2b7e151628aed2a6abf7158809cf4f3c'))
+        iv = bytes.fromhex('000102030405060708090a0b0c0d0e0f')
+        cipher = bytes.fromhex('7649abac8119b246cee98e9b12e9197d5086cb9b507219ee95db113a917678b2')
+        self.assertEqual(aes.cbc(cipher, iv).hex(),
+                         '6bc1bee22e409f96e93d7e117393172aae2d8a571e03ac9c9eb76fac45af8e51')
+        self.assertEqual(aes.ecb(cipher[:16]), aes.cbc(cipher[:16], bytes(16)))
+
+    def test_rejects_partial_blocks_and_bad_keys(self):
+        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, 'key must be'):

+        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, 'whole blocks'):

+        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, 'whole blocks'):
+            AesDecryptor(bytes(16)).cbc(b'x' * 16, b'iv')
+
+
+if __name__ == '__main__':
+    unittest.main()

+"""Read-only XDVDFS (Xbox/Xbox 360 game partition) directory reader.
+
+Layout readings, checked against the Midnight Club: Los Angeles disc: the game
+partition starts at a fixed image offset per disc generation; its volume
+descriptor is sector 32 of the partition and carries `MICROSOFT*XBOX*MEDIA` at
+both ends, then the root directory sector and size. A directory is a binary
+search tree of 4-byte-aligned records: left and right subtree offsets in dwords,
+start sector, size, attribute byte (0x10 = directory), name length and name.
+Records never cross a sector boundary; 0xFF bytes pad the rest of a sector.
+"""

+import struct
+
+SECTOR = 2048
+MAGIC = b'MICROSOFT*XBOX*MEDIA'

+PARTITIONS = (('XGD2', 0xFD90000), ('XGD3', 0x2080000), ('XGD1', 0x18300000), ('plain', 0))
+DIRECTORY = 0x10
+MAX_DIRECTORY = 64 * 1024 * 1024
+MAX_ENTRIES = 1_000_000
+
+
+def safe_component(name):
+    if (not name or name in ('.', '..') or len(name) > 255 or '/' in name or '\\' in name

+        raise ValueError('unsafe XDVDFS name')
+    return name

+
+class XdvdfsDisc:
+    """Lists every file and directory; reads payloads by entry. Never writes."""

+    def __init__(self, path):
+        self.path = Path(path)
+        if self.path.is_symlink():
+            raise ValueError('linked disc input')
+        self.stream = self.path.open('rb')
+        self.size = self.path.stat().st_size
+        try:
+            if self.size % SECTOR:
+                raise ValueError('truncated disc image')
+            for generation, base in PARTITIONS:
+                if base + 33 * SECTOR > self.size:
+                    continue
+                descriptor = self.read_at(base + 32 * SECTOR, SECTOR)
+                if descriptor[:20] == MAGIC:
+                    if descriptor[0x7EC:0x800] != MAGIC:
+                        raise ValueError('XDVDFS descriptor trailer mismatch')
+                    break
+            else:
+                raise ValueError('no XDVDFS volume descriptor')

+                if previous['sector'] * SECTOR + previous['size'] > current['sector'] * SECTOR:

+++ b/tools/xex2.py

+"""Minimal XEX2 (Xbox 360 executable) image loader: normal/no encryption, basic packing only.
+
+Header readings (big-endian), checked on the MCLA `default.xex`: `XEX2`, module flags,
+PE data offset, reserved, security-info offset, optional-header count, then (key, value)
+pairs. Optional header 0x3FF (file format info) gives encryption type (0 none, 1 normal)
+and compression type (1 basic: (data, zero-fill) block pairs). The security info carries
+the image size at +4 and the AES-128 file key at +0x150. The session key is the file key
+decrypted under the retail key with AES-ECB; the image is AES-CBC with a zero IV.
+
+The retail key is the public XEX2 key used by open-source Xbox 360 emulators (Xenia
+`src/xenia/cpu/xex_module.cc`, `xe_xex2_retail_key`). LZX ("normal") packing is not implemented.
+"""
+import struct
+
+from aes_decrypt import AesDecryptor
+
+RETAIL_KEY = bytes.fromhex('20b185a59d28fdc340583fbb0896bf91')
+FORMAT_INFO = 0x3FF
+MAX_IMAGE = 256 * 1024 * 1024
+
+
+def load_image(xex):
+    """Return (image bytes, facts) for a basic-packed XEX2; raises on anything else."""
+    if len(xex) < 24 or xex[:4] != b'XEX2':
+        raise ValueError('not an XEX2 executable')
+    _, pe_offset, _, security, count = struct.unpack_from('>IIIII', xex, 4)
+    if not 24 + 8 * count <= pe_offset <= len(xex) or not security + 0x160 <= pe_offset:
+        raise ValueError('XEX2 header outside file')
+    headers = dict(struct.unpack_from('>II', xex, 24 + 8 * i) for i in range(count))
+    if FORMAT_INFO not in headers:
+        raise ValueError('XEX2 file format info missing')
+    at = headers[FORMAT_INFO]
+    size, encryption, compression = struct.unpack_from('>IHH', xex, at)
+    if compression != 1:
+        raise ValueError('only basic XEX2 packing is supported')
+    if encryption not in (0, 1) or size < 8 or (size - 8) % 8 or at + size > pe_offset:
+        raise ValueError('unsupported XEX2 file format info')
+    blocks = [struct.unpack_from('>II', xex, at + 8 + 8 * i) for i in range((size - 8) // 8)]
+    image_size = struct.unpack_from('>I', xex, security + 4)[0]
+    if not 0 < image_size <= MAX_IMAGE or sum(d + z for d, z in blocks) != image_size:
+        raise ValueError('XEX2 block sizes disagree with image size')
+    payload = xex[pe_offset:]
+    stored = sum(d for d, _ in blocks)
+    cipher = (stored + 15) & ~15 if encryption else stored  # AES works on whole 16-byte blocks
+    if cipher > len(payload):
+        raise ValueError('XEX2 payload shorter than its blocks')
+    if encryption:
+        session = AesDecryptor(RETAIL_KEY).ecb(xex[security + 0x150:security + 0x160])
+        payload = AesDecryptor(session).cbc(payload[:cipher])
+    image, position = bytearray(), 0
+    for data, zero in blocks:
+        image += payload[position:position + data]
+        image += bytes(zero)
+        position += data
+    if image[:2] != b'MZ':
+        raise ValueError('XEX2 image is not a PE (wrong key or packing)')
+    pe = struct.unpack_from('<I', image, 0x3C)[0]
+    if image[pe:pe + 4] != b'PE\0\0':
+        raise ValueError('XEX2 image lacks a PE header')
+    return bytes(image), {'image_bytes': image_size, 'encryption': encryption, 'compression': compression,
+                          'blocks': [list(b) for b in blocks]}
